open.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
If you've come about the roaring, I've had the council, I've had the cafe, and I've had a man from the Chronicle who thought a tiger was a lion. Ray Tulloch. Keeper.
sf_keeper
He's fed, he's watered, he's not in season and he's not in pain. He stands at the sea wall at three and I stand with him. That's all either of us knows.
miriam
Twenty years with tigers and he's reporting it like a symptom. Good. That's a man I can work with.

passives.line: Boots still wet from the sea-wall side, and he hasn't slept. He stood with the tiger last night and the night before. He is not a man who believes it's the tide.
The feeding board says 3AM five nights running and under the fifth there's a ruled line and a time: 0312. He timed something. He didn't write what.

options.text: We're not the council. Tell us about him. The male.
Five nights. You're not sleeping either, Mr Tulloch.
(Look at the tiger. Let him look at you.)

kind.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
Raj. Bengal, nine years, came from Chessington with a bad leg and a worse temper and he's the gentlest thing on this front, present company included.
sf_keeper
He doesn't pace. That's the thing. A tiger that's upset paces. He stands and he listens, and I've never seen a tiger listen.

hard.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
No. And you can put that in whatever you're writing. The keeper's not sleeping. Neither's the keeper's wife, neither's the cafe.
sf_keeper
The animals come first. When they sleep, I sleep. Ask what you came to ask.

silent.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
...He's looking at you. He doesn't look at the public.
sf_keeper
Right. You can stay. He's a better judge than me and he's decided.

hub.speaker: sf_keeper
hub.prompt: Ask. The lemurs want feeding at six and they don't care what you are.
lines: sf_keeper
Ask. The lemurs want feeding at six and they don't care what you are.

static.line: 0312. He timed it. He heard it with the soles of his feet through the slab and the tiger heard it first. Ask him what it said.

options.text: The tiger house is on the fort's footings. What's under the slab, on the sea side?

fail.line: Concrete and granite and a Victorian drain. You want geology, there's a man at the library. I keep cats.

options.text: Let us in at three. We'll stand at the wall with you both.
0312, on the board. You timed something. What did you hear, Ray, through your boots?
The lab says the fur on your fence is Raj's. From the brush you hang there.
We'll let you feed the lemurs.

rock.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
The old magazine tunnels. Granite-lined, they run from under the tiger house out toward the cliff, and the Trust bricked the far end in '74 and painted the brick.
sf_keeper
I've been down the near end with a torch. It's dry. It's dry and it's warm, and granite's not warm, and the warm end's the sea end.
june
A granite tunnel that's warm at the sea end. That's a conductor, not a cave. I'd like a meter on that slab.

three.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
...Side gate, ten to three. No torches, he doesn't like torches. No talking. You stand where I put you and if he turns round you don't.
sf_keeper
I'll be honest with you. I'd like somebody else there. I'd like somebody else to hear it, so it's not just me and him.
elijah
He's been alone with it five nights. That's a long time to be the only one who hears.

three_fail.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
No. Public's out at six and that's the public, and four strangers at a tiger wall in the dark is how a keeper loses his job and a tiger.
sf_keeper
Brenda at the cafe hears it through her floor. Go and sit up with her. She'd like the company.

heard.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
...Three notes. Up through the slab, into the boots. Then a click, like a dial going round, then three notes again.
sf_keeper
Twelve minutes past three, and it went for an hour and stopped.
sf_keeper
Raj heard it at three. I heard it at twelve past, because I'm a man and I'm slow. He looked at me when I got it, like, there, now you know.
sf_keeper
I don't put that on a board. I put a line and a time. You've got the rest now and I'd like you to take it away with you.
dale
Three notes and a click. That's the same thing the cave's meant to do. It's under the whole front.

heard_fail.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
I timed when he lay down. That's what keepers do. We write down when they lie down.
sf_keeper
You want noises, the coastguard at Culver's got a set that picks up everything. Go and bother him. He's awake, he's always awake.

fur.speaker: sf_keeper
lines: sf_keeper
Ha. Did they. Good. Twenty quid of lab to find out I hang a brush on a fence.
sf_keeper
You're the first lot who checked. The Chronicle had it as a second tiger loose on the front. I've got one tiger and he's standing right there not being loose.
miriam
One explanation down, honestly, and he's grateful for it. That's worth more than the fur.
